title: 开发板：PWM 预习和 ADC
summary: PWM 引脚在 0 和 3.3 V 之间快速切换：万用表读到平均值，示波器看到方波。ADC 引脚把 0–3.3 V 量成 0–4095 的数。
description: 这一课先预习 PWM（5.8 细讲）：同一个引脚，万用表读到平均值，示波器看到方波。然后学本单元的主角 ADC：引脚把 0–3.3 V 的电压量成 0–4095 的数。电路：GPIO2（PWM）→ 330 Ω → 红色 LED → GND；10 kΩ 电位器接在 3V3 和 GND 之间，滑动端接 GPIO34（ADC）。

cards.title: 两块表，两个答案
text: 这一课先**预习 PWM**（5.8 会细讲），再学本单元的主角 **ADC**。
先让一个引脚用 PWM 点亮 LED，然后**用两种仪表看同一个引脚**：万用表和示波器。
两个读数对不上。到底谁说的是真话？

cards.title: PWM 是快速开关，ADC 是一把尺子
text: - **PWM**：引脚每秒开、关 1000 次。开的时候是满电压，关的时候是 0。“开”占一个周期的比例叫**占空比** D。
![](fig:pwm)
- 万用表反应慢，只读到**平均值**；示波器看到真实的方波。两个都对：
$$V_{avg} = D × V_{high}$$
- 代入数字：D = 75 %，高电平约 3.3 V，$V_{avg} = 0.75 × 3.3 ≈ 2.5$ V。LED 的亮度也跟着平均值走。
- **ADC** 反过来：它把引脚上 0–3.3 V 的电压**量成一个数**，从 0 到 4095，像一把有 4096 个刻度的尺子。
![](fig:adc)

cards.title: 换占空比，再接一个旋钮
text: - 换几个占空比，看三样东西怎么变：LED 的亮度、万用表的读数、方波的宽度。
- 然后接一个**电位器**当可调的分压器：滑动端的电压送进 ADC 引脚。
- ADC 引脚最多只能接 3.3 V。比它高的电压要先分压——下一个实验就做这件事。

cards.title: 带走
text: - **PWM 不改变高电平，只改变“高”的时间比例。** 万用表读平均值，示波器看真实波形。
- PWM 每次“高”时，电流和常亮时一样大：它不能绕过引脚的电流上限。
- **ADC 把 0–3.3 V 量成 0–4095。** 超过 3.3 V 会损坏引脚。ESP32 只有 GPIO32–39（ADC1）能和 Wi-Fi 同时用。
- 真实的坑：ESP32 的 ADC 在接近 0 V 和 3.3 V 的两头不线性，还有噪声。项目里要校准，多读几次取平均。

caption.text: 占空比 75 %：每个周期里 3/4 的时间是高电平。万用表读到的是虚线那个平均值。

i18n.en: Duty cycle 75 %: three quarters of every period is high. The multimeter reads the dashed average.

caption.text: 0 V 读 0，3.3 V 读 4095，中间按比例。超过 3.3 V，引脚就有危险。

i18n.en: 0 V reads 0, 3.3 V reads 4095, and everything in between in proportion. Above 3.3 V the pin is in danger.

en.title: Dev board: a first look at PWM, then the ADC
en.summary: A PWM pin switches quickly between 0 and 3.3 V: the multimeter reads the average, the scope shows the square wave. An ADC pin measures 0–3.3 V as a number from 0 to 4095.
en.description: This lesson previews PWM (unit 5.8 covers it properly): on the same pin the multimeter reads an average and the scope shows a square wave. Then comes the unit's main topic, the ADC: a pin that measures 0–3.3 V as a number from 0 to 4095. Circuit: GPIO2 (PWM) → 330 Ω → red LED → GND; a 10 kΩ potentiometer between 3V3 and GND, its wiper to GPIO34 (ADC).
steps: Pick **ESP32 dev board DevKitC** and click **`b1`**: the two rows of pins go into b1–b19 and i1–i19. USB is plugged in by default, so the board is powered.
GPIO2 has only one free hole, **`a15`**. A **jumper** **`a15`** → **`a20`** brings it out to column 20, so the resistor, the probes and the scope all have room.
**Resistor** **`330 Ω`** in **`c20`**–**`c23`**; **red LED** long lead **`d23`**, short lead **`d26`**; blue **jumper** **`a26`** → **`tn26`**.
**Click the board** and, in the pin list under Properties, set **GPIO2** to **PWM**. Click the row to open it: duty cycle **`25 %`**, frequency **`1 kHz`**. The LED lights, but dimly.
**Multimeter**: red probe on **`b20`**. It reads much less than the pin's 3.3 V.

**Scope** probe: tip on **`e20`**, ground clip on **`tn18`**. Look at the trace: the voltage only jumps between two values. If the scope window covers the board, press **▾** at its top right to fold it, or drag its title bar away.
Set the duty cycle to **`75 %`**. The LED gets brighter and the multimeter reads three times as much; on the scope the square wave is just as tall, only wider.
Set the duty cycle back to **`25 %`**.
**Potentiometer** (**`10 kΩ`**): click **`h22`**; its three legs sit in h22, h23, h24. Blue **jumper** **`j22`** → **`bn22`** (GND), red **jumper** **`j24`** → **`bp24`** (3V3).

Wiper to GPIO34: **jumper** **`g23`** → **`j5`** (GPIO34 is column 5 of the bottom row). Set **GPIO34** to **ADC**: the row shows the ADC voltage and a reading from 0 to 4095. **Drag the potentiometer** and watch the number follow.
Press **Check my circuit**, then answer the measurement questions with the scope, the multimeter and the pin list.
hints: A multimeter's DC range reads the average: average = duty × high level.
On the scope the high level equals the pin voltage when fully on; PWM only changes the fraction of time spent high.
ADC reading = voltage / 3.3 V × 4095; with the wiper in the middle the voltage is half of 3.3 V.
tests: PWM lights the LED; the ADC reads the wiper voltage

measurements.explain: The square wave jumps between 0 V and the high level: 3.3 V minus the drop across the output resistance.
The DC range reads the average: 0.25 × 3.2 V ≈ 0.80 V.

measurements.ask: The LED's average current (click the LED and read the current under Properties)
measurements.explain: 0.25 × 4.1 mA ≈ 1.0 mA; during the 25 % of the time it is high, it is still 4.1 mA.

measurements.ask: Wiper at 50 %: the voltage on GPIO34 (the ADC voltage in the pin list, or the multimeter)
In the same state, about what is GPIO34's 12-bit raw ADC reading?
measurements.explain: 1.65 / 3.3 × 4095 ≈ 2048: 12 bits = 4096 levels, with 3.3 V at full scale.

cards.title: Two meters, two answers
text: This lesson first **previews PWM** (unit 5.8 covers it properly), then turns to this unit's main topic, the **ADC**.
First let a pin light an LED with PWM, then **look at that one pin with two instruments**: the multimeter and the scope.
The two readings disagree. Which one is telling the truth?

cards.title: PWM is a fast switch, an ADC is a ruler
text: - **PWM**: the pin switches on and off 1000 times a second. On, it is at full voltage; off, at 0. The fraction of each period that is "on" is the **duty cycle** D.
![](fig:pwm)
- A multimeter is slow and only reads the **average**; the scope shows the real square wave. Both are right:
$$V_{avg} = D × V_{high}$$
- With numbers: D = 75 %, a high level of about 3.3 V, $V_{avg} = 0.75 × 3.3 ≈ 2.5$ V. The LED's brightness follows the average too.
- An **ADC** works the other way round: it **measures** the pin's 0–3.3 V **as a number** from 0 to 4095, like a ruler with 4096 marks.
![](fig:adc)

cards.title: Change the duty cycle, then add a knob
text: - Try a few duty cycles and watch three things change: the LED's brightness, the multimeter reading, the width of the square wave.
- Then add a **potentiometer** as an adjustable divider: its wiper voltage goes into the ADC pin.
- An ADC pin takes 3.3 V at most. A higher voltage has to be divided down first — the next lab does exactly that.

cards.title: Take away
text: - **PWM leaves the high level alone and changes only how long it is high.** The multimeter reads the average, the scope shows the real waveform.
- Every "high" of a PWM pin carries the same current as a steady high: PWM is no way round the pin's current limit.
- **An ADC measures 0–3.3 V as 0–4095.** More than 3.3 V damages the pin. On the ESP32 only GPIO32–39 (ADC1) work while Wi-Fi is on.
- A real-world catch: the ESP32's ADC is not linear near 0 V and near 3.3 V, and it is noisy. Real projects calibrate it and average several readings.

tests.name: PWM 点亮 LED；ADC 读到滑动端的电压

measurements.explain: 方波在 0 V 和高电平之间跳：高电平是 3.3 V 减去输出电阻上的压降。

measurements.ask: 万用表：GPIO2（第 20 列）对 GND 的电压
LED 的平均电流（单击 LED 看「属性」里的电流）
电位器滑动端在 50 %：GPIO34 的电压（看引脚列表的 ADC 电压，或用万用表）
同一状态下，GPIO34 的 12 位 ADC 原始读数大约是多少？

steps.text: 选**「ESP32 开发板 DevKitC」**，单击 **`b1`**：两排针插进 b1–b19 和 i1–i19。USB 默认插着，板子已经通电。
GPIO2 只有 **`a15`** 一个空孔。**跳线** **`a15`** → **`a20`** 把它引到第 20 列：电阻、表笔和探头就都有地方插了。
**单击开发板**，在「属性」的引脚列表里把 **GPIO2** 设成 **PWM**。单击这一行展开：占空比 **`25 %`**，频率 **`1 kHz`**。LED 亮了，但比较暗。
**万用表**红表笔点 **`b20`**。它读到的电压，比引脚的 3.3 V 小得多。
**示波器**探头：针尖 **`e20`**，接地夹 **`tn18`**。看波形：电压只在两个值之间跳。示波器窗口挡住面包板时，点它右上角的 **▾** 收起，或拖标题栏挪开。
占空比改成 **`75 %`**。LED 变亮，万用表读数变成三倍；示波器上方波的高度没变，只是变宽了。
滑动端接 GPIO34：**跳线** **`g23`** → **`j5`**（GPIO34 在下排第 5 列）。把 **GPIO34** 设成 **ADC**：这一行显示 ADC 电压和 0–4095 的读数。**拖动电位器**，看数字跟着变。
点**「检查我的电路」**，再用示波器、万用表和引脚列表回答测量题。

hints: 万用表直流档读的是平均值：平均 = 占空比 × 高电平。
示波器上的方波高电平和常亮时的引脚电压一样，PWM 只改变“高”的时间比例。
ADC 读数 = 电压 / 3.3 V × 4095；滑动端在中间时电压是 3.3 V 的一半。
